title: Read Daniel's hand edit to Obstacle Set
tier_reason: reading his edit and writing down what it implies — nothing to walk back
ask: Daniel hand-edited Obstacle Set in the sprite editor and said he was fixing: "Space between the fenceposts is transparent again — the middle band was opaque white". The measurement: Obstacle Set: 14 pixels across 1 frame (frame 5). Colors dropped: #f8f4e6. The silhouette moved, not just the interior shading. Look at it against the style guide draft and the rest of the sheet, and say in a few lines what his edit is telling you about the direction — whether it agrees with the guide, quietly contradicts it, or repeats something he has done before. If it is just tidying and there is nothing to learn, say exactly that in one line; a short honest answer beats manufactured significance. Do not propose amendments to the guide yet; he wants a look session before it is signed. This is evidence-gathering for that session.
first_action: Open assets/sprites/generated/obstacles.png and the ledger entry (step 3) in HQ, compare it with the style guide in docs/design/09-art-direction.md, and write down what the edit says about his taste.

result:
Cell 4 of that sheet is the fence — the boundary tile, and since yesterday's ruling the one she builds herself (`world/farm.gd:345`). The 14 pixels sit at x 4–10, y 7–8: a 7×2 band straight across the middle of the tile, between the posts. The colour he dropped, `#f8f4e6`, is not in the style guide and is not in the ambient palette. It is the generator's paper backdrop, baked opaque into the cell.

**What the edit says about the direction: nothing new.** It agrees with the guide rather than bending it. The guide is silent on negative space, but its contrast rule — the ambient world stays low-contrast pastel and the tappable things hold the saturated pixels — is the same instinct. `#f8f4e6` is lighter than every colour the guide names, so a slab of it inside a prop is the brightest thing on screen sitting on the one object that is supposed to read as a line you can see through. He's not restyling. He's removing something the pipeline put there.

**What it does say is that we have a defect, not a taste question.** This is the same edit for the second time today: 16:36 and 22:04, identical frame, identical 14 pixels, identical bounding box, identical colour. His own note says "again". In between, at 16:37, he pulled `#f8f4e6` and `#bfd470` out of the two gate cells — same category, grass and paper baked into props. (`#bfd470` is the guide's grass base one step darker in red, which is the channel shift the art-direction chapter already records — not drift.)

Both times, the same two follow-ups were filed: a keying step for the pipeline to Ravi, a sweep of the shipping sheets to Yuki. Neither exists in the repo — there is no background-keying step anywhere in `tools/`, and the sheets still carry the fill. So he has now hand-cleaned the same fence tile twice while the fix sat unbuilt, and nobody has asked the obvious question: what re-baked those 14 pixels after he had already erased them at 16:36.

The one thing worth carrying into the look session is smaller and quieter: of the thirteen cells on that sheet, he keeps going back to the fence and the gates. Not the rock, not the tree. He wants the boundary to read as a line you see past, not a wall. That's staging for the captures, not an amendment.

**What accepting this starts:** Ravi finds out what restored the pixels and builds the keying step; Yuki cleans the sheets already in the build. Both land before anyone renders a look-session capture.
